pack.title: Texting games
pack.description: Set a communication boundary without debating affection.

scenarios.setting: Someone you are dating expects instant replies while you are at work.
scenarios.jab: If you liked me, you'd reply faster.
scenarios.goal: Set a communication boundary without debating affection.

replies.line: I like you. I can't text continuously while I'm working.
replies.why: It affirms the relationship while stating a practical limit.
replies.delivery: Keep the affection warm and the work boundary matter-of-fact; avoid apologizing for working.

replies.line: I'm working. I'll reply this evening.
replies.why: It gives a clear expectation without accepting the guilt framing.
replies.delivery: Keep the affection warm and the work boundary matter-of-fact; avoid apologizing for working.

replies.line: I enjoy talking to you; work takes my attention, so let's catch up tonight.
replies.why: It offers connection at a realistic time rather than constant access.
replies.delivery: Keep the affection warm and the work boundary matter-of-fact; avoid apologizing for working.

replies.line: My phone has office hours too.
replies.why: Humor makes your availability boundary feel ordinary rather than punitive.
replies.delivery: Keep the affection warm and the work boundary matter-of-fact; avoid apologizing for working.

followUp.jab: It takes two seconds to answer.
followUp.line: Sometimes I can answer quickly; you can't rely on that during work.
followUp.why: It acknowledges occasional availability without turning it into an obligation.
followUp.delivery: Keep the affection warm and the work boundary matter-of-fact; avoid apologizing for working.
